blocks.text: Jeremiah 1 first places the prophet in a defined setting: Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, is associated with priests at Anathoth, and the heading spans from Josiah’s reign to Jerusalem’s exile. Against that extended crisis, the call narrative presents Jeremiah as appointed before birth, reluctant to speak, and commissioned to speak words placed in his mouth. His work is described in paired terms: uprooting, breaking down, destroying, and overthrowing, but also building and planting. The commission therefore includes both severe judgment and constructive renewal.

Jeremiah 1 is the opening of a book that brings together several forms of material, including poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, oracles concerning nations, and an appendix. A practical outline places this opening chapter before major collections of Jeremiah’s messages and narratives. The book’s varied shape should therefore be read as a collection with differing kinds of material, rather than as one uninterrupted account.
